MFR wins POSCO contract for robotic steel-plate spacer placement

The system combines autonomous travel, 3D vision and manipulation to place wooden spacers around heavy steel plates.

Electronic Times ↗2 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 2

Automating a hazardous handling step

MFR, a company founded by a DGIST researcher, announced on October 2 that it won a POSCO supply project for placing wooden spacers between thick steel-plate products during warehouse shipping operations. The work brings people close to heavy plates. The company describes the project as nearing final preparation for introduction at the site.

Navigation followed by manipulation

Sensor fusion and optical tracking support travel and obstacle avoidance. At the work position, AI and 3D vision identify the plate geometry and location before the arm places a spacer. An adjustable lifting mechanism and multi-axis control address higher positions. Automatic charging and wireless supervision let operators monitor from outside the hazardous area.

Site performance remains to be proven

The contract is a significant step, but it is not evidence of completed full-scale operation. MFR plans to validate safety and usefulness in the steelworks before extending the approach to heavy-load handling, large plants and specialized manufacturing. The report supplies no measured cycle time, placement-success rate or accident reduction.
